front: Mesdames et Messieurs, bonsoir.
back: Good evening, ladies and gentlemen.
context: The classic opening of a speech. Note the liaison: mesdames-z-et.

front: Je serai bref.
back: I'll be brief.
context: A promise speakers rarely keep!

front: Permettez-moi de commencer par une anecdote.
back: Let me begin with an anecdote.
context: Stories capture an audience better than statistics.

front: Imaginez un instant un monde sans frontières.
pronunciation: [ee-mah-zhee-nay zan nan-STAHN an mohnd sahn frohn-TYEHR]
back: Imagine for a moment a world without borders.
context: Inviting the audience to picture something.

front: Soyons clairs : cette situation ne peut plus durer.
pronunciation: [swah-yohn KLEHR : set see-tü-ah-syohn nuh puh plü dü-RAY]
back: Let's be clear: this situation cannot go on.
context: 'Soyons' = imperative of être (let's be).

front: Ne nous y trompons pas : l'enjeu est historique.
pronunciation: [nuh noo zee trohm-POHN PAH : lahn-ZHUH eh tees-toh-REEK]
back: Make no mistake: what's at stake is historic.
context: 'Ne nous y trompons pas' = let us not be fooled.

front: Il ne s'agit pas de punir, mais de prévenir.
pronunciation: [eel nuh sah-zhee pah duh pü-NEER, meh duh pray-vuh-NEER]
back: It's not about punishing, but about preventing.
context: 'Il ne s'agit pas de… mais de…' reframes a debate.

front: Qui peut sérieusement croire que rien ne changera ?
pronunciation: [kee puh say-ryuhz-mahn krwahr kuh ryan nuh shahn-zhuh-RAH]
back: Who can seriously believe nothing will change?
context: A rhetorical question: no answer expected.

front: Je ne parlerai pas de ses échecs passés.
pronunciation: [zhuh nuh par-luh-reh pah duh say zay-shek pah-SAY]
back: I won't mention his past failures.
context: 'La prétérition': saying you won't mention something, while mentioning it.

front: Va, je ne te hais point.
back: Go, I do not hate you.
context: Chimène in Corneille's 'Le Cid': the textbook 'litote', meaning 'I love you'.

front: Ce n'est pas mal du tout.
back: That's really rather good.
context: A litote: understatement to say more. Very French.

front: Moi président de la République, je ne serai pas le chef de la majorité.
pronunciation: [MWAH pray-zee-DAHN duh lah ray-pü-BLEEK, zhuh nuh suh-reh pah luh shef duh lah mah-zhoh-ree-TAY]
back: As President of the Republic, I will not be the head of the majority.
context: François Hollande's 2012 debate anaphora: he repeated 'Moi président' fifteen times.

front: L'anaphore consiste à répéter un mot en début de phrase.
pronunciation: [lah-nah-FOR kohn-seest ah ray-pay-tay an MOH ahn day-bü duh FRAHZ]
back: Anaphora consists in repeating a word at the start of each sentence.
context: A favorite device of political orators.

front: Permettez-moi d'insister sur ce point.
back: Allow me to stress this point.
context: 'Insister sur' = to emphasize.

front: Je ne le répéterai jamais assez.
back: I can't say it often enough.
context: Emphasis through apparent modesty.

front: J'irai même plus loin.
back: I'll go even further.
context: Building up an argument.

front: C'est précisément là que le bât blesse.
pronunciation: [seh pray-see-zay-MAHN lah kuh luh bah BLES]
back: That's exactly where the problem lies.
context: 'Le bât' = a pack saddle. 'Là où le bât blesse' = the sore point.

front: Les faits sont têtus.
back: Facts are stubborn things.
context: Used to dismiss an opponent's spin.

front: J'en appelle à votre sens des responsabilités.
pronunciation: [zhahn nah-pel ah voh-truh sahns day res-pohn-sah-bee-lee-TAY]
back: I appeal to your sense of responsibility.
context: 'En appeler à' = to appeal to.

front: Le moment est venu d'agir.
back: The time has come to act.
context: A typical call to action at the end of a speech.

front: Il sait captiver son auditoire.
back: He knows how to captivate his audience.
context: 'L'auditoire' = the audience (of a speech).

front: C'est un orateur hors pair.
back: He's an exceptional speaker.
context: 'Hors pair' = unrivaled.

front: Son discours a galvanisé la foule.
back: His speech electrified the crowd.
context: 'Galvaniser' = to galvanize, fire up.

front: J'ai le trac avant chaque intervention.
back: I get stage fright before every talk.
context: 'Le trac' = stage fright, nerves.

front: Marquez une pause avant votre argument principal.
back: Pause before your main argument.
context: Silence is a rhetorical tool.

front: Je vous rejoins sur ce point.
back: I agree with you on that point.
context: 'Rejoindre quelqu'un' = to agree with someone (formal).

front: Je ne vais pas me dérober à votre question.
pronunciation: [zhuh nuh veh pah muh day-roh-bay ah voh-truh kes-TYOHN]
back: I'm not going to dodge your question.
context: 'Se dérober' = to evade.

front: Il a botté en touche.
back: He sidestepped the question.
context: 'Botter en touche' (rugby: kick the ball into touch) = to evade.

front: C'est de la langue de bois.
back: That's just political waffle.
context: 'La langue de bois' (wooden tongue) = empty official jargon.

front: Le ministre s'en tient aux éléments de langage.
pronunciation: [luh mee-NEES-truh sahn tyan oh zay-lay-mahn duh lahn-GAHZH]
back: The minister is sticking to the talking points.
context: 'Les éléments de langage' = prepared talking points.

front: Ce n'est pas tout à fait exact.
pronunciation: [suh neh pah too tah feh teg-ZAKT]
back: That's not quite accurate.
context: A polite correction.

front: Je ne peux pas vous laisser dire cela.
pronunciation: [zhuh nuh puh pah voo leh-say deer suh-LAH]
back: I can't let you say that.
context: A firm interruption in a televised debate.

front: Vous me faites un procès d'intention.
back: You're attributing intentions to me that I don't have.
context: 'Un procès d'intention' = judging someone on presumed motives.

front: Je n'ai jamais prétendu une chose pareille.
pronunciation: [zhuh neh zhah-meh pray-tahn-dü ün shohz pah-RAY]
back: I never claimed any such thing.
context: 'Une chose pareille' = such a thing.

front: La question ne se pose pas en ces termes.
pronunciation: [lah kes-tyohn nuh suh pohz pah ahn say TEHRM]
back: That's not the right way to frame the question.
context: Reframing a hostile question.

front: Je prends acte de vos critiques.
back: I take note of your criticism.
context: 'Prendre acte' = to acknowledge formally.

front: Je comprends votre colère, et je la partage.
pronunciation: [zhuh kohm-prahn voh-truh koh-LEHR, ay zhuh lah par-TAHZH]
back: I understand your anger, and I share it.
context: Acknowledging emotion to defuse a tense exchange.

front: Je maintiens ce que j'ai dit.
back: I stand by what I said.
context: 'Maintenir' = to maintain, stand by.

front: Ce n'est pas le sujet.
back: That's not the issue.
context: Steering back to the topic (can sound abrupt).

front: Il y a un malentendu.
back: There's a misunderstanding.
context: 'Un malentendu' = a misunderstanding.

front: À cet égard, les chiffres sont éloquents.
pronunciation: [ah set ay-GAR, lay SHEE-fruh sohn tay-loh-KAHN]
back: In this respect, the figures speak for themselves.
context: 'Éloquent' = telling, eloquent.

front: Je vous renvoie la question.
back: I'll turn the question back on you.
context: A debate tactic.

front: Je le dis avec gravité.
back: I say this with all seriousness.
context: Signaling a solemn moment.

front: Ensemble, nous pouvons relever ce défi.
back: Together, we can rise to this challenge.
context: 'Relever un défi' = to take up a challenge.

front: Je vous remercie, et vive la République !
pronunciation: [zhuh voo ruh-mehr-SEE, ay veev lah ray-pü-BLEEK]
back: Thank you, and long live the Republic!
context: French presidential speeches end with 'Vive la République ! Vive la France !'
